  ### ***Component 2 \- Edges: Predicates*** {#component-2---edges:-predicates}

  #### **2a. Big picture: Uses/functions of predicates** {#2a.-big-picture:-uses/functions-of-predicates}

  **C2a-1.** Predicates operate on sets of entities  (2 or more)

  	Includes Traditional RDF *\<subject, predicate, object \>* triples, or sets of entities in tuples  connecting N\>2 entities 

  ? a.k.a. Subject.predict \= model.object , or Predicate(subject)=object syntax?  with…

  **C2a-2.** Function as **directed** or **undirected** edges (or paths in the case of tuple/N-ary predicates) 

  E.g. parent/child would naturally define a sense of a directed edge

  E.g. edges that might define synonyms between two “category” type entities,  e.g. \<also\_known\_as\>, would be undirected 

  This will impact how queries maybe handled, shortcuts for declaring edges 

  **C2a-3.** May entail constraints on the entity class/ nodes in the  “predicate path” / nodes that the predicate edge connects

  Parent/child can only connect entities of the same “entity class type” where that means something TBD…

  E.g. synonym/”also\_known\_as” predicate may imply same “entity class type” at some lower level

  are only allowed to  connect certain node classes (or their Class descendents) 

  E.g.  ? **C2a-9** ?  Only special types of entities can be bound to actual data or literals  ?? (binding is a SPECIAL sort of predicate)

  **C2a-4** Each maps to a set of constraints on *relationship networks* they can be part of 

  A parent/child directed set of relationships includes defining a DAG

  **C2a-5** API’s to allow  “navigation” rules or query types

  	I.e. find the cousins or siblings of an entity relative to a parent/child relationship 

  **C2a-6** May come in sets and definition and a one way ordered relationship should imply another:

  	E.g. parent/child  \<entity1, parent, entity2 \> (i.e.parent(entity1, entity2))  should also define \<entity2, child,entity1\>

  	E.g. also\_known\_as \<entity1,  also\_known\_as, entity2\> in the model also implies \<entity3,  also\_known\_as, entity1 \>

  **C2a-7 (related to**  **C2a-5** ) May “imply” symmetric, transitive or commutative logic/rules for queries 

  Maybe special “is a part of” for features of part type objects would be transitive

  		\< entity1, contains, entity2\>, \<entity2, contains, entity3 \>  \=\> \< entity1, contains, entity3\>

  		Facilitates queries up an entire tree “all stuff that has a leaf as a part”

   ?**C2a-8** Predicates relation returns as entities?? 

  	Allows compound facts 

  This would allow multi-part facts to be considered entities …. I.e. Not ( Species1, Has(leaf\_type, compound)  ).... Can think of others ….


  #### **2b. Predicates for Single Edges/Pairs and for N-tuple “facts” /Paths**  {#2b.-predicates-for-single-edges/pairs-and-for-n-tuple-“facts”-/paths}

  	**Usually** 

  * P0: A binding:  Assigns the value of a literal   
    * (i.e. integer 3, or string “blah” OR binds to external data OR is set by a config)   
    * P1: A SINGLE edge between two nodes:  \<entity, entity\> \-  
      * Single edge  
      * Fits standard “RDF” / \<subject, predicate, object\> use case   
    * P2: A PAIR of edges \- i.e. this predicate connects three nodes   \<entity1, entity2, entity3\>  
    * P3: A TRIO of edges \- connects four nodes   \<entity1, entity2, entity3, entity4\>

## **Data Asset Sketches** {#data-asset-sketches}

### ***Asset 1: Source*** {#asset-1:-source}

- The place data is sourced by Arborphy  
- When linked across other data sources, indicates ‘coherence’  
  - E.g. a single list of species that by implication come from some sort of coherent taxa hierarchy 

  ### 

  ### ***Asset 2: Taxa hierarchy*** {#asset-2:-taxa-hierarchy}

- Description: iNat observations and ecosystem descriptions focus on species as “identifiers” and “components” ….  
  - Living things like plants and animals, are commonly identified with groups like species – well, specifically, as species, which are meant to allow individual instances to be compared with other similar living things that exist in different places & times ….  
    - “A taxonomic unit, whether named or not: i.e. a population, or group of populations of organisms which are usually inferred to be phylogenetically related and which have characters in common which differentiate (q.v.) the unit (e.g. a geographic population, a genus, a family, an order) from other such units.” per Wikipedia  
  - Ever  
- that are grouped into species   
- Groups and subgroups that meant to be useful ways of comparing instances of living things over space and time  
  - Examples Focusing for now on botanical taxa with intention to expand   
    - Include Biological Taxa hierarchies, Ecosystem hierarchies (e.g. from the US National Vegetation Classification System, see [Data Sources - Databases, Sites, Books](https://docs.google.com/document/u/0/d/1_dx5yi2YzGx8eyjnPIQ2TmvTBYW3Kf0ks16a7SFcO4U/edit))   
- Sample dataset overview:   
  - *Traditional Biological Taxa have the form of a hierarchy:*  
    - *Domain → Kingdom → Phylum/Division → Class → Order → Family → Genus → Species → (Subspecies/Variety/Form, Cultivar)*  
1. *Domain* \[Eukarya\]   
2. *Kingdom* \[Plantae, Fungi, Animalia\]   
   1. Marchantiophyta (liverworts) — https://www.gbif.org/species/9  
   2. Anthocerotophyta (hornworts) — https://www.gbif.org/species/13  
   3. Bryophyta (mosses) — https://www.gbif.org/species/35  
   4. Tracheophyta (vascular plants) — https://www.gbif.org/species/134281921  
3. *Phylum/Division*    
4. *Class*  
5. *Order*   
6. *Family*   
7. *Genus*   
8. *Species* \-or- hybrid of species   
9. *Subspecies and/or Variety and/or Form and/or Cultivar*  
   - Multiple hierarchies exist even with the same leaf node (tho leaf nodes can split)  
     -   
   - MOdel may need to simultaneously reference multiple hierarchies  
   - For Arborphy, will identify hierarchy by a single source for an entire hierarchy  
     - E.g. iNaturalist as of date  
   - Botanical/Naturlist Sources  identify each node in each taxa hierarchy with a publication source*,*   
     - *E.g. iNaturalist*

   ### ***Asset 2: Taxa List**  \[Sets of Taxa that’s coherent relative to some system \]* {#asset-2:-taxa-list-[sets-of-taxa-that’s-coherent-relative-to-some-system-]}

- Context: We’ll often have a list of species that dont’ have traces to a coherent/cited hierarchy or cladeogram  
- A list of taxa (e..g species) that are identified with some taxa hierarchy OR POSSIBLY just with a source (i.e. the taxa hierarchy may consist ONLY of the species).   
- A coherent set of taxa hierarchies as of a point in time  
- May map to a set of species   
- E.g. an iNat download from a date in December 2026 (as we have) is a Taxa vocabulary   
  - It’s a set of species, and all the hierarchy that each maps to   
  - That hierarchy was coherent AS OF the download date  
  - Qualitvatively: …a download on a different date might have some species moved around

  ### ***Asset 3:Features, Values, Feature-Value vocabularies \**** {#asset-3:features,-values,-feature-value-vocabularies-*}

  	\\{Feature\_j, Value\_{j,k}\\}  where j \<= NFeatures, k\<= NValue\_{Feature\_j}

    * Feature\_j, is some set of features, e.g. “Leaf Type”  
      *  Newcomb four features: “Flower Symmetry”, “Plant Type”, “Leaf type”, “Leaf arrangement”   
    * Value\_{j,k}  \\in { V\_{1},..,V\_{N\_{feature}}}

        * Feature\_3 \= “Leaf Type”,   
          * NValue\_{Leaf\_type} \= 3,    
          * Value\_3,j \= { “No apparent leaves”, “Leaves entire”, “leaves toothed or lobed”, “leaves divided”}  
        * Feature\_2 \= “Plant Type”   
          * Value\_2 \= {“Shrubs”, “Vines”,“Wildflowers \- No apparent leaves”, “Wildflowers \- Basal leavesOnly” , “Wildflowers \- Basal Leaves Only", "Wildflowers \- Opposite or Whorled Leaves”}

## **Model Sketch**  {#model-sketch}

### ***M-0. Big picture view:***  {#m-0.-big-picture-view:}

- This model is meant to contemplate lots of ways of grouping individual items \- especially living things \- that exist in instances that are transient in time, but where groupings like botanical taxons help connect over those instances…  
  - But we may need to look at lots of these in parallel  
  - Goal:  
    - Have versions of each of the assets that correspond to different core sources, combine them   
      - That might mean we have multiple species-\>feature/value mappings, corresponding to different keys….   
    - 

  ### ***M-1. Some entity superclass starters and intended uses:***  {#m-1.-some-entity-superclass-starters-and-intended-uses:}

  * **Superclass1** : Entities for stuff that refers to natural things outside of specific instances in space/time , like   
    * Call it: **ObjectGroup/OG** \- examples will include botanical taxa or com “OG”’s of some sort are all related to some reference source   
  * **Superclass2**: Base entities for features and parts/subparts  (e.g. leaves, leaf margins, pedicules, pediculate )  
    * Call it**: FeatureOrPart/FG**    
    * Constraint: every class in Superclass 1 has to have a connection with something in superclass 1   
      * Feature only meaningful  if it is related to a plant part or plant   
  * **Superclass 3:**  Base entities for tracking what sort of vocabulary or sources are being referred to  
    * Call it**:  ReferenceFrame**  
    * Can be used to switch bindings and even instantiated OG & FP hierarchies   
      * E.g. Some date of iNat for species \-\> taxa hierarchies  
      * E.g. Newcomb \- species,feature,value set  – 

  ### ***M-2. Some predicates and intended uses:***  {#m-2.-some-predicates-and-intended-uses:}

  * Predicate vocabularies   
    * E.g. P1: parent/child \- Constraints  
      * \<e1, parent, e2 \> \=\> \<e2, child, e1\>   
        * Statement of one means model implies the other   
        * DAG structure across connected edges of this predicate type   
        * Implies subject/object are in some sense of the same “type”   
          * I.e. same entity parent superclass??  
      * Functionality \-common iterators  
        * Children,   
        * Siblings, cousins  
        * parents  
      * ? Verbalization alternatives   
        * “Parent”/”child”  
        * “Part of”/“has Part”  
        * ? maybe a reference the something about the subject/object entity types

	Every **ObjectGroup** and **FeatureorPart** must have a  **ReferenceFrame**

### ***Zhu etal 2024  Multi-Modal Knowledge Graph Construction and Applications: A Survey \[[airXiv link](http://arxiv.org/abs/2202.05786)\]*** {#zhu-etal-2024-multi-modal-knowledge-graph-construction-and-applications:-a-survey-[airxiv-link]}

- Multimodal Knowledge graphs are constructed of text and images   
  - Goal of MMKG is to e.g. facilitate extraction of the attributes and relationships that correspond to visual phenomena  
    - e.g.  partOf (e.g., The keyboard and the screen are parts of a laptop.) and  
      - e.g. colorOf (e.g., A banana is usually yellow or yellowish-green but not blue).  
    - Natural fit for many naturalist/botanical sources that use words to describe instances of plants that occur in time \- and \-space, and are most directly captured with images  
- Core KG definition has   
  - ***G*** \= { ***E, R, A, V, T\_{R}, T\_{A}*** }

    Graph \= {

    {*Entities/Concepts **(E)***, 

    Predicates/Relations/”Edge Concepts” ***(R)***, 

    Attributes ***\[A\]***,  \[special predicates that link to literal attribute values \- BINDINGS \]

    Literal attribute values ***\[V\]***,  \[data bound or ‘instance variables’ assigned in code\]

    …this paper focuses on these can be multi-modal /complex data types 

    Relation Triples ***T\_{R} \= R x E x E*** 

    Attrubute Triples ***T\_{R} \= R  x A x V***

    ***}***

    ***\=***  

    ***E, R, A, V, T\_{R}, T\_{A}*** }

    

    

  - Multimodal graphs admit “data items in a modality other than text”  
    - ***A-MMKG***: Either as entity values (i.e.  ***A \= A\_{KG}*** U ***A\_{MM}  ) ,** where {KG} denotes simple data, and {MM} multi-modal data in the form of images or sound*   
      - Attribute: , an image is associated with an entity, like the Eiffel  tower and Eiffel.jpg  
    - ***N-MMKG***: Alternatively, multi-modal data can sit on separate entities, ***E \= E\_{KG}*** U ***E\_{MM}***  
      - Since multi-modal data are treated as new entities, more inter-modal and intra-modal relations are discovered and added into the MMKG   
      - Image associated with text entity in “ImageOf” relation  
      - Two images can also be associated in one of the following relations: 1\) contain: One image entity visually contains another image entity by the relative position of images. 2\) nearBy: One image entity is visually nearby another image entity in an image. 3\) sameAs: Two different image entities refer to the same entity. 4\) similar: Two image entities are visually similar to each other.  
      - In addition, in N-MMKGs an image is usually abstracted into several image descriptors, which are usually summarized into feature (?attribute?) vectors of the image entity  
      - Typical multi-modal tasks with images and texts include image caption \[32\], visual question answering \[33\], and cross-modal retrieval \[34\], etc.  
      - before MMKGs, people mainly focus  
      - on multi-modal learning, and more recently the ***Vision and Language Pre-trained Models (VL-PTMs)***, which will be briefly introduced below  
    - ***N-MMKG*** examples  
      -  IMGpedia \[25\] links images from Wikimedia Commons1 to DBpedia via the structured Wikipedia data in RDF format already extracted in DBpedia Commons \[26\], which additionally adds the similarity relations between images.  
      -

  ### ***Suchanek etal, 2024 YAGO 4.5: A Large and Clean Knowledge Base with a Rich Taxonomy \[[arXiv pdf link](https://arxiv.org/html/2308.11884v2) \]*** {#suchanek-etal,-2024-yago-4.5:-a-large-and-clean-knowledge-base-with-a-rich-taxonomy-[arxiv-pdf-link-]}

- Why interesting   
  - YAGO is \[wikipedia/wiki data\] “cleaned up” (e.g. cycles removed, redundant synonyms removed, empty concepts removed)  
    - Product of a research collaboration  
    - They publish the methodology and probably the code   
    - Persisted on Zenodo \[a research persistence toolkit that spans data & code … European consortium that shares both code & data for research \]  
  - YAGO is a useful model as input to JM thesis & ARborQuest data model   
  - YAGO is an example of a KG with relevant features  
    - Separation of Entities/Concepts & Data/Facts    
    - A hierarchy of Entities/Concepts with inheritance   
    - A data model that   
      - includes constraints (which are in a language called SHACL (sp?))  
      - based on a consortium/open standard WC3   
      - maintained by a research group with published ‘cleanup’’ 

  ### ***Razniewski etal 2024 Completeness, Recall, and Negation in Open-world Knowledge Bases: A Survey \[[link](https://dl.acm.org/doi/pdf/10.1145/3639563)\]*** {#razniewski-etal-2024-completeness,-recall,-and-negation-in-open-world-knowledge-bases:-a-survey-[link]}

- Definition:  
- Knowledge bases are comprised of   
  - **“Fact”/”Relation” Tuples  / Triples**  
    - **〈s\_{subject}, p\_{predicate}, o\_{object}〉 ∈ (E ) ×  P × (E ∪ L) \= (Entity)  x Predicate x (Entity ∪ Literal )**  
    - Sometimes with special reserved predicates    
      - **Subclass/subcategory predicate: 〈s\_{child\_entity},** *subclass\_of* **, o\_{object\_entity}〉 ∈ E × E**  
      - **Type/ instance of predicate: 〈s\_{instance\_entity},** *type* **, o\_{object\_entity}〉 ∈ E × E**  
    - **QUESTION**  
      - How do entities treated as classes correspond to instances?  
  - **Negative “Fact” Tuples**  
    - ¬**〈s, p, o〉= NOT ( 〈s, p, o〉)** *e.g. \<Stephen\_Hawking, awarded\_prize, Nobel\_Prize\>*  
  - built on three pairwise disjoint unbounded sets   
    - **Inheritance as a special predicate:**  
      - **E (Entities) and Entity “Classes”**  
      - Entities refer to uniquely identifiable objects  
      - Entities defined in classes   
      - Classes can be arranged in a subclass hierarchy.  
      - An entity can be an instance of a class, and this can be expressed by a triple with   
      - the predicate type, as in   
        - 〈Entity\_name, **type**, **Entity\_Class** 〉  
      - Some KBs allow specifying constraints, such as domain and range constraints on predicates, functionality constraints, or disjointness constraints between classes, usually in a formalism called Description Logic \[14\]  
    - **P (predicates), and**   
      - Predicates (also known as relations, properties, or attributes) link an entity to another entity or to a literal.  
      -   
    - **L (literals)**  
  - Specification may also include constraints  
    - E.g. domain and range constraints on predicates, functionality constraints, or disjointness constraints between classes,  
    - See e.g. Baeder 2003 The description logic handbook: Theory, implementation and applications
